main_body: Two logs lying horizontally, stacked. Light round cut ends face west, and dark bark bodies extend east.
top_band: none: column x=11 runs dark brown bark from row 4 to row 13 with no lighter horizontal surface. Column x=7 meets the light cut end face (rows 4-8, L 216-170) and then dark bark.
evidence: The logs are drawn as a side profile. The round end caps are vertical faces seen from the west, and the bark bodies are dark with no lighter top plane. Nothing reads as a horizontal surface seen from above. The light band in column x=4 is the end-grain disc, not a top. This is a side elevation with an end face, so the top surface is missing.

style.evidence: The end grain has about 4 tones plus ring dots, which reads reasonably. The bark is only 2-3 very dark browns (#8b6435, #502e15, #1a0c04) with little grain or highlight. The outline is a tinted dark brown (#2c1709), so the sticker look is avoided, and 5x5 flat-fill coverage is 0%. The piece has only 9 distinct colours and 9 colours per tile, against 38-40 distinct colours and 17-20 per tile for the references. That is markedly thinner than the references, and the bark mass is murky and under-modelled.
